judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in the same Grade R (rank 0), Term 4, Emergent Reading, Phonological/Phonemic Awareness table row (page 55), so direction rests on substantive content rather than coordinate gap. The first statement, 'Recognises sounds at the beginning of some words' (LC tags: beginning sounds, phonemic awareness), isolates only the initial phoneme of a word. The second, 'Relates sounds to letters and words and understands that words consist of more than one sound: duck is d-u-ck - done aurally', decomposes into two LCs (sound-letter correspondence; full aural segmentation of a whole word into its constituent sounds) and therefore requires attending to all phonemes in sequence and mapping them to letters. Hearing an initial sound is the narrower capability whose proficiency supports success in full aural segmentation and sound-letter linking, so the developmental direction runs first to second within the same term; this is substantive extension, not mere repeated wording (token overlap is limited to generic 'sounds/words/of'). Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), so the judgment rests on the printed statement text and LC metadata supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R (rank 0), Term 3, Emergent Reading Skills, so direction rests on substantive content, not rank. The first SFI has children divide multisyllabic words into syllables using claps/drumbeats and count the syllables (LCs tagged syllables, clapping, counting, phonological awareness) — segmentation of spoken words into larger sub-word units. The second SFI requires understanding that a word consists of more than one sound, with phoneme-level exemplification ('hand' = h-a-n-d), a finer-grained analysis unit under the 'Relates sounds to letters and words' sub-strand. Facility with clapping and counting syllable chunks supports the more demanding insight that words break into individual sounds, so proficiency in the first supports success in the second within the same term; this is a substantive shift from syllable to phoneme granularity rather than repeated wording (token overlap is only the word 'words'). Same-term direction is permitted under the Grade/Term ordering rule. Endpoint source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both endpoints and their ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, so this judgment rests on the bounded excerpts supplied.

Shared LC tokens ('listening', 'questions') and the shared Grade 3 ancestor alone were not treated as sufficient; the judgment rests on the statement texts and term coordinates. A buildsTowards from the Term 2 role-play statement to the Term 3 fine-motor statement is not supported (the motor-strengthening work underpins writing rather than the reverse), and the only pedagogically plausible dependency direction (Term 3 fine motor to Term 2 role-play writing) would be a backward within-grade direction and is therefore invalid. relatesTo records the genuine same-skill-area complementarity without asserting sequence. Identical wording, shared ancestors, shared Learning Component and rank-gap-0 proximity cannot by themselves establish developmental dependency, so buildsTowards is not warranted and the symmetric relatesTo (null direction, canonical order preserved) is the correct complete judgment. judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R Skills (rank 0) but sit in different skill areas and terms: the first is Term 2 Emergent Writing / Handwriting ('Develops fine-motor control by playing more finger rhymes with finger actions'), the second is Term 1 Listening and Speaking / Daily activities ('Sings simple songs and does actions (with help)'). Their substantive coherence is the shared rhyme-and-song-with-actions practice (LC tags 'actions', 'finger rhymes' vs 'actions', 'songs', 'movement'), where accompanying songs and rhymes with physical actions reinforces the same classroom routine and body/hand coordination. However, the intended learning targets differ in kind: the Term 1 statement is an oral-language/participation outcome done with help, while the Term 2 statement targets fine-motor control for emergent handwriting; the evidence does not show that proficiency in singing songs with actions substantively supports success in developing fine-motor control, so a Term 1 to Term 2 buildsTowards is not warranted on this evidence. Symmetric relatesTo reflects the meaningful reinforcement without asserting dependency. Both endpoints' source evidence excerpts are truncated (24 omitted items each) and ancestors carry merge/audit context, which limits but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade 2 (rank 2) Reading and Phonics, but in different terms and sub-strands: the second is Term 1 / Phonics ('Uses initial and final consonant blends to build up and break down words such as bl-a-ck, bri-ng, sa-ng', with LCs tagged blending/segmenting/consonant blends), while the first is Term 4 / Group Guided Reading ('Continues to build a sight vocabulary from the incidental reading programme, the graded reading series and high-frequency word lists', LC tagged sight vocabulary/high-frequency words/reading). The overlap is not mere repeated wording ('build', 'words'); it is a decoding-to-automatic-word-recognition progression across distinct sub-strands. Evidence limits noted: both endpoints have truncated source evidence (and the first also truncated LC evidence), so the judgement rests on the bounded statement text, LC tags and resolved Grade 2 coordinates supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade R (rank 0) Emergent Reading. The first is Term 2 under Sub-strand 'Phonological/Phonemic Awareness': listening for the odd word in a sequence where all words begin with the same sound and judging whether two given sounds are the same or different (/c/,/c/ vs /c/,/g/) — purely aural sound discrimination. The second is Term 3 under Sub-strand 'Relates sounds to letters and words': recognising sounds at the beginning of some words such as friends' names or animal names, i.e. applying initial-sound awareness to specific, meaningful spoken words within a sub-strand that links sounds to letters and words. The Term 2 discrimination of same/different beginning sounds is the aural foundation that supports the Term 3 identification of initial sounds in named words, and the direction Term 2 -> Term 3 is a permitted earlier-to-later term progression within one grade. This is substantive extension (from odd-one-out/same-different judgements to naming initial sounds in real-word contexts), not mere repeated wording, although the shared tokens ('beginning', 'sounds', 'listening') alone were not treated as sufficient. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and both carry upstream audit/merge context, so the judgement rests on the full statement texts and identity-scope fields supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both are Listening and Speaking (Oral) Skill statements in the same strand. The first is Grade R, Term 1, 'Listens without interrupting' (rank 0), carrying the single LC 'Listens without interrupting'. The second is Grade 1, Term 4 (rank 1), 'Listens without interrupting, taking turns to speak and asking questions for clarification.', decomposed into three LCs: the same non-interrupting listening component plus 'Takes turns to speak' and 'Asks questions for clarification'. This is substantive expansion across grades, not mere repeated wording: the later statement retains the Grade R attentive-listening behaviour and extends it to reciprocal turn-taking in talk and active clarification questioning. Secure non-interrupting listening in Grade R supports success with the broader Grade 1 Term 4 interactive oral expectation, so the lower-rank statement builds towards the higher-rank one. Endpoint source excerpts and LC metadata are truncated, but the untruncated statement texts and resolved Grade coordinates are sufficient for this judgment.

One asks learners to recognise onset and rime in more complex blend patterns (dr-eam, scr-eam, str-eam); the other to recognise vowel digraphs and diphthongs ('oy', 'oi', 'ay', 'ai'). With identical Grade rank (2) and identical Term, there is no substantive evidence for a developmental direction, so symmetric conceptual coherence is the supported judgment. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), which limits but does not contradict this reading.

The shared evidence is only the general notion of 'words' plus weak token/trigram overlap ('words', 'than') and a shared Grade R ancestor, which alone is not developmental evidence. Aural segmentation of spoken words does not specifically underpin tracking printed words during shared reading, and the printed-word behaviour does not presuppose phoneme segmentation; they are complementary word-awareness skills within the same Grade R Emergent Reading programme, so symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment rather than a Term 2 to Term 4 buildsTowards. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream audit/merge context, so a stronger dependency claim is not warranted on this bounded evidence.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit under the same Grade 2, Term 1, Reading and Phonics / 'Daily Phonic Activities of 15 minutes:' sub-strand (identity scope grade 2 | term 1 | phonics), so shared placement alone is not decisive. The pair-specific evidence is substantive: the first statement revises decodable word families with short vowel sounds (-at, -ag, -am, -it), while the second applies that same daily phonics content to weekly spelling of ten words 'taken from phonics lessons'. Secure recognition and manipulation of these short-vowel rimes directly supports accurate spelling of the weekly phonics word list, i.e. the first supports likelihood of success in the second within the same term (permitted earlier/same-term direction). The reverse direction is weaker: spelling ten words a week presupposes, rather than establishes, the word-family patterns. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream audit/merge context, so confidence is moderate rather than high.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade 1, Term 3 (same grade rank 1, same Term ancestor 840dec6b), but in different skill areas: the first is a Shared Reading (Reading and Phonics) bullet 'Recognises cause and effect in a story', the second a Listening and Speaking (Oral) bullet 'Sequences pictures of a story and matches captions with the pictures'. They cohere substantively as complementary narrative-comprehension work on the same shared token 'story' (LC tags: comprehension/cause and effect/story vs sequencing/pictures/story; captions/matching), with ordering of story events and causal reasoning reinforcing each other. The evidence does not, however, show that proficiency in either is a developmental support for the other: they are concurrently taught, same-term, cross-modal (oral picture sequencing vs text-based shared reading inference), with no increase in complexity, independence or scope between them, so same-rank directional buildsTowards is not substantively supported. Source evidence for both endpoints and the second endpoint's LC metadata are truncated, and both carry upstream audit/merge context, so judgment rests on the bounded statement text, identity scope and LC tags supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills are printed bullets in the same Grade 1 / Term 4 / WRITING / 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' table row (window 25, page 81), with identical resolved coordinate Grade 1 (rank 1) and identical ancestry, so no rank or term difference supports a developmental direction. Substantively they are complementary components of the same emergent composing task: writing at least three sentences of own news or a creative story using taught sounds, sight words, capital letters and full stops, versus beginning to use present and past tense correctly in writing. LC tags overlap only on 'writing' (punctuation/sentences/sight words vs grammar/tense), indicating distinct but mutually reinforcing facets of connected text production rather than one being a prerequisite for the other; the evidence shows no expanded capability or dependency in either direction. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), which limits any stronger claim, so symmetric coherence is the supported judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are the identical printed bullet 'Reads aloud to a partner' under Reading and Phonics / Paired-Independent Reading in Term 3, one at Grade 2 (resolved coordinate rank 2) and one at Grade 3 (resolved coordinate rank 3). The bounded evidence shows the same daily 20-minute paired/independent reading routine in both grades with no visible change in text demand, independence, or scope; all nomination signals are pure similarity (Jaccard 1.0 on tokens, trigrams, LC text and tags, one shared LC) plus a weak grade-rank proximity signal. Repeated wording plus a grade-rank gap does not establish the substantive extension required for buildsTowards in this deliberately repetitive CAPS framework. The recurrence is nevertheless more than generic repetition: it is the same specific partner oral-reading practice inside the same named sub-strand and term, so proficiency reinforcement and instructional coherence are pair-specific, supporting canonical symmetric relatesTo with null direction. Limitations: both endpoints' source evidence (24 omitted items each) and the shared LC metadata are truncated, so a finer grade-level differentiation in the full source cannot be ruled out; all endpoints and the eight grouping ancestors carry upstream merge/audit context (benign banner and sub-strand merges with resolved ancestry, unresolved_ancestry false throughout), retained below.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R, Term 4 (same canonical rank 0, same Term node d7f3920f), but in different Skill Areas: Emergent Reading / Shared Reading ('Makes links to own experience when reading with the teacher, viewing television or pictures') and Emergent Writing ('Draws pictures to convey a message about a personal experience and uses this as a starting point for writing: with help adds a word, phrase or sentence'). They share the substantive pedagogical thread of connecting personal experience to pictures and texts — receptive meaning-making from pictures/shared reading alongside expressive use of a drawing about a personal experience to launch emergent writing — which is genuine reading–writing complementarity rather than mere wording overlap (shared tokens are limited to 'experience', 'pictures', function words). Within the same Grade and Term, and across distinct skill areas, there is no source-backed evidence that proficiency in one is developmentally required for or substantively deepens into the other, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Note that both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and the second endpoint's LC evidence is truncated, so some corroborating detail is outside this bounded excerpt.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 1 Skills about answering questions, but they differ substantively in demand and context. The first (Grade 1, Term 1, Listening and Speaking (Oral), 'Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities') is oral answering of simple questions such as those about personal details; LC tags: answering, oral, personal details, questions. The second (Grade 1, Term 2, Reading and Phonics, Shared Reading) requires answering 'a wide variety of types of questions based on the texts read including higher order type questions'; LC tags: comprehension, higher order, questions, reading. This is an expansion from familiar personal-knowledge oral responses to text-based comprehension across varied and higher-order question types, so fluency in the Term 1 oral question-answering routine plausibly supports success with the Term 2 shared-reading comprehension questioning. Direction is earlier Term 1 to later Term 2 within the same Grade 1 coordinate (rank 1), which is permitted. This is an inferred curriculum-grounded relation; both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each), so judgement rests on the supplied statement text, identity scopes and Learning Components.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R, Term 2, EMERGENT WRITING, sub-strand 'Emergent Writing:' Skill bullets from the same printed table cell, with identical resolved coordinate rank (Grade R) and term, so no rank-based developmental direction is available. Substantively they are complementary emergent-literacy behaviours: spontaneously copying environmental print during play (LC tags: copying print, environmental print, play) and attributing meaning to one's own letters/squiggles (LC tags: pretend reading, letters, squiggles). Each reinforces the understanding that marks carry meaning, but neither statement's text shows expanded scope, greater independence, or dependency over the other, so a same-term buildsTowards is not warranted; the shared Skill Area/Sub-strand and page proximity alone would not establish a relation, but the pair-specific print-meaning coherence supports relatesTo. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and carries upstream merge/audit context, which limits but does not contradict this reading.
